approach: Stop rewriting the local branch after a merge, so a running job's base stays an ancestor of HEAD and `plan` still lands it. Delete the `resync_onto_merge` call, the function and `resync_tip`. Move the squash-conflict fix to the pull request head: at publish time `land_pr` cuts the head from the local landed commit by replaying it onto the host's current default-branch tip (`Git::replay`). Commits that an earlier squash already carries replay to empty and are skipped, so each merge lands one job as one commit. The local source commit is stored in `PrLink`, so reruns do not re-cut or re-push. A fingerprint check guards the push. Stale jobs keep today's `plan` handling. Update the docs, D103 and the changelog.

decisions.choice: Dispatch from the local branch HEAD as today, but never rewrite that branch on merge; cut each pull request head onto the remote default tip at publish time.
decisions.reason: Dispatch records base_commit = head, and `plan` in land.rs needs the base to be an ancestor of HEAD. Only `resync_onto_merge` breaks that on a merge. Removing it makes dispatch independent of any merge, and the replay primitive already exists.

rejected.option: Dispatch from a pinned ref such as origin/main or a new refs/athena/base
rejected.why: Job records are committed to the local branch and read from HEAD by Records::load; a second base would split the record history. Larger and riskier.

rejected.option: Keep resync but run it only when no job is running
rejected.why: That is the wait the request wants removed, and it needs a cross-process view of running jobs.

rejected.option: Merge the squash commit into the local branch
rejected.why: Adds merge commits, failing the no-extra-merge-commit criterion.

rejected.option: Re-cut the head on every `land --pr` rerun
rejected.why: Replay makes new timestamps, so each rerun would replace-push; storing the source in PrLink avoids that.

decisions.choice: Add `source: Option<String>` (serde default) to PrLink and a defaulted `Remote::cut_head(base_branch, commit)` overridden by GitRemote; compare source (falling back to head) with the local landed commit.
decisions.reason: A default returning the commit unchanged keeps existing fakes and old links working.

rejected.option: Replay in Athena::land_pr before calling the flow
rejected.why: The default branch name is read inside publish, and the replace path needs the same cut; one place is easier to test.

decisions.choice: If the cut head's fingerprint differs from the verified one, or replay conflicts, push nothing and report; the job is handled as stale and Athena never merges it.
decisions.reason: Keeps P5 and the merged-unverified protection and honors the out-of-scope on automatic merge or re-verification.

rejected.why: Out of scope; would land content no verifier saw.

decisions.choice: Edit gh.rs even though it is not in the listed deliverables (finding 2).
decisions.reason: The only call to resync_onto_merge, the Remote trait, publish and replace_head live in gh.rs, so the fault cannot be fixed from the listed files alone. The edit is minimal: remove one call, add one trait method with a default, use it in two places. The plan flags this to the reviewer as a necessary scope extension, and run.rs and watcher.rs are left untouched unless a real reference is found.

rejected.option: Confine the change to the listed files by making resync_onto_merge a no-op in land.rs
rejected.why: Leaves dead code and a misleading call, and the squash-conflict fix still needs the cut in the publish flow.

steps: Read gh.rs tests (FakeRemote, Racy, the bare-candidate-head rerun test) to see how fakes and links are built.
In pr.rs add `source: Option<String>` with #[serde(default)] to PrLink; fix constructors.

In gh.rs add Remote::cut_head with a default returning the commit; implement it in GitRemote (ls-remote tip, ensure_commit, return unchanged if tip is an ancestor, else replay from the merge-base with signs_commits).
In publish and replace_head call cut_head, check fingerprint equals the verified one (bail if not), push, store source; in land_pr compare source (fallback head) with job.commit.
Remove the resync_onto_merge call; delete resync_tip and resync_onto_merge and their tests from land.rs; update the header.
Add the criterion 1 test in land.rs and the criterion 2 test in gh.rs; confirm they fail when the cut or no-rewrite is undone.
Run cargo fmt --all, cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings, cargo test --locked; grep that resync_onto_merge is gone from crates/.

risks.risk: A cut head carries different content than the verified landed commit.
risks.mitigation: Fingerprint check before any push; mismatch or replay conflict pushes nothing and reports; merged-unverified check stays.

risks.risk: Reruns re-cut and push a new head each time.
risks.mitigation: Store head and source in PrLink; reuse unless the source commit changes.

risks.risk: Existing gh.rs fakes and tests break from the new trait method or field.
risks.mitigation: Defaulted method and serde default; keep the 'rerun replaces a bare candidate head' test passing.

risks.risk: Local branch diverging from main surprises the maintainer.
risks.mitigation: Docs state it; plan uses ancestry of the job's own base, unaffected.

demonstrations.method: New land.rs test with a real git repo (Git::isolated): job B verified at base P; job A lands on top of P locally; a squash merge of A is simulated on a side ref (single-parent commit with A's tree). Then run the merge-time path and check nothing changed.
demonstrations.observes: Local HEAD id is equal before and after the merge; B's base and worktree files are unchanged; P is an ancestor of HEAD; `plan` for B returns Plan::Tree with the verified fingerprint, so its candidate lands as one commit with no Stale outcome.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the resync still rewriting the branch, B's base is no longer an ancestor of HEAD, so `plan` returns Stale and the unchanged-HEAD and Plan::Tree assertions fail.

demonstrations.method: New gh.rs test with a bare remote and GitRemote: local branch holds P, A's landed commit, a records commit, B's landed commit (back to back, before any merge). Cut A's head with cut_head, simulate A's squash merge on the remote default branch, then cut B's head.
demonstrations.observes: Each cut head is a linear chain onto the then-current remote tip; `git rev-list --merges` is empty; B's head holds only B's own commits, not A's; cut tree fingerprints equal the verified ones; local branch tip is unchanged.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the replay onto the remote tip, B's head would carry A's local commit, the new-commit count would exceed the job's own commits, and the commit-count and merge-free assertions fail.

demonstrations.method: Run the three Athena checks over the whole workspace, including the two new tests and the rewritten former resync tests.
demonstrations.observes: cargo test exits 0 with the new tests passing; `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check` also exit 0.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the resync call were removed but resync_tip/resync_onto_merge left behind, clippy -D warnings fails on dead code; if the cut or no-rewrite behavior were missing, the criterion 1 and 2 tests fail so cargo test fails; unformatted code fails fmt --check.
